```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
have_stack <- all(vapply(
  c("projectData", "monocle3", "BPCells", "SingleCellExperiment",
    "SummarizedExperiment", "Matrix"),
  requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE
))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = have_stack)
```

This vignette explains what `projectData.monocle3` stores, what it does when a
CDS is loaded, and how long the restored files live. The task-oriented guides are
`vignette("authoring-monocle3-data", package = "projectData.monocle3")` and
`vignette("using-monocle3-data", package = "projectData.monocle3")`.

## What is stored

`save_monocle_cds()` stores a CDS with Monocle's own persistence API,
`monocle3::save_monocle_objects()`, with no tar archive. The package does not
implement a serializer of its own. In the data package, the directory
`inst/extdata/<name>/` holds

* `file_index.rds`, Monocle's index of what was saved;
* `cds_object.rds`, the CDS without its counts matrix (metadata, reductions,
  models, in-memory assays and alternative experiments);
* `bpcells_matrix_dir/`, the BPCells directory that holds the counts.

| Representation | Handling |
|---|---|
| `counts` as a BPCells directory matrix (`MatrixDir`), including a lazily subset one | Saved as it is, through native Monocle saving |
| `counts` as `dgCMatrix` / `dgTMatrix`, or a BPCells in-memory matrix | Converted to a BPCells directory automatically, on a **copy**; your CDS is not modified |
| Other in-memory assays (`logcounts`, `spliced`, ...) | Retained, stored inside `cds_object.rds` |
| In-memory alternative experiments (`altExp()`, for example ADT or CRISPR), at any depth | Retained |
| Cell and gene metadata, reductions, `metadata()` | Retained |
| A secondary assay (main CDS or any alternative experiment) that is stored on disk: BPCells, HDF5 or `DelayedArray` | **Refused** before anything is written (`projectData.monocle3_external_assay`) |
| `counts` as a dense matrix, `DelayedMatrix`, HDF5-backed BPCells, or missing | **Refused** before anything is written |
| A CDS saved with `hdf5_assays = TRUE`, a tar archive, or with in-memory counts | **Rejected** by the loader at validation |
| More than one CDS per resource | Not supported |

Alternative in-memory assays and alternative experiments were tested with
synthetic data; other `SingleCellExperiment` extensions are not assumed to be
supported. Unsupported storage is refused, never silently converted or left
pointing at files that your users do not have. The adapter never converts a
secondary assay for you, because that could need a lot of memory.

### Why independently disk-backed assays are refused

Monocle saves a BPCells assay other than the managed `counts` only as a
*reference* to the directory it was created in. The package would install, and
the reference would dangle on every other machine. Convert such assays to
in-memory matrices, or drop them.

## Restoring a CDS

Restoration happens on first access, in two stages. The core (projectData)
controls when, how often and where; the adapter controls how.

1. **Validation** (adapter, `validate`) inspects the installed directory without
   building the CDS or reading matrix values. It reads `file_index.rds`, requires
   exactly one rds-format CDS and one BPCells matrix directory, rejects absolute
   or `..` paths and symbolic links, and checks that every listed file and every
   file BPCells writes is present. It runs before every uncached opening.
2. **Opening** (adapter, `open`) calls `monocle3::load_monocle_objects()` on the
   installed directory, with the BPCells location set to the working directory
   that projectData allocated for this opening, and checks that the result is a
   `cell_data_set`.

A demonstration:

```{r demo, message = FALSE}
library(monocle3)
library(projectData)
source(system.file("examples", "demo-package.R", package = "projectData.monocle3"))

work <- file.path(tempdir(), "storage-demo")
dir.create(work)
lib <- file.path(work, "library")
dir.create(lib)
invisible(demo_data_package(work, lib, name = "demoMonocleData"))
data_config(messages = FALSE)

installed <- file.path(lib, "demoMonocleData", "extdata", "demo_cds")
before <- tools::md5sum(list.files(installed, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE))
wd <- getwd()

cds <- data_get("demo_cds", package = "demoMonocleData", lib.loc = lib)
```

### Where the files go

Native Monocle loading does **not** use the installed BPCells directory in
place: it copies it. Monocle requires the target directory to exist and creates
uniquely named `monocle.bpcells.<date>.<id>.tmp` directories in it, so the adapter
passes the allocated working directory directly. Two copies are made: the counts
and a second, row-ordered copy that Monocle keeps in the `counts_row_order`
assay (the BPCells layout differs between them).

```{r workdir}
work_root <- file.path(tempdir(), "projectData-work")
copies <- list.files(work_root, pattern = "tmp$", recursive = TRUE,
                     include.dirs = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
basename(copies)
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(cds)
```

The working directory is unique to this opening, under the session temporary
directory (`file.path(tempdir(), "projectData-work")`; projectData encodes the
collection and resource names in the directory names). The counts really are read
from the copy rather than from the installed package:

```{r backing}
count_dir <- BPCells::all_matrix_inputs(SummarizedExperiment::assay(cds, "counts"))[[1]]@dir
startsWith(normalizePath(count_dir), normalizePath(work_root))
```

and the installed resource was not touched, nor was your working directory:

```{r untouched}
identical(before, tools::md5sum(list.files(installed, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)))
identical(wd, getwd())
```

The adapter never calls `setwd()`, never writes to the installed package (which
is treated as read-only and immutable, and may really be on a read-only file
system), and refuses a working directory that lies inside the installed
resource. Because both matrices are restored there, the installed package is not
needed for the counts once the object is open. One thing is not copied: if the
CDS has a UMAP model, its Annoy nearest-neighbour index is memory-mapped by
Monocle from the installed file. On Linux that keeps working if the package is
removed while the object is in use, since an unlinked file stays mapped; that is
platform behavior, not a guarantee. Do not reinstall or remove a data package
while a CDS from it is in use, and note that Windows cannot remove a mapped file.
(The model also records the original install path as informational metadata;
nothing reads it.)

### Disk-backed does not mean free

"Disk-backed" means the matrix data can stay on disk. It does not mean RAM-free
or free of temporary disk costs:

* The cell and gene metadata, reductions, models, and every other assay are
  ordinary R objects in memory.
* Computations that collect the counts (for example converting to a
  `dgCMatrix`) read them into memory.
* Every opening makes **two copies** of the matrix in the session temporary
  directory, in addition to the installed one. Attach, detach and attach again
  makes another pair; nothing is shared between openings. There is no persistent
  cache in this version, so every new session copies again on first access.

```{r size}
sum(file.size(list.files(copies, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)))
sum(file.size(list.files(file.path(installed, "bpcells_matrix_dir"), full.names = TRUE)))
```

(The first is the working copies, the second one installed copy; for realistic
datasets expect about twice the installed matrix per opening.)

## Lifetime and detachment

* Monocle removes the restored directories when R exits, through its own exit
  hook. The adapter does not delete anything: not on `data_detach()`, not when
  objects are removed, not with `on.exit()`, because a retained CDS may still
  reference them.
* `data_detach()` forgets the collection and cached objects. A CDS you kept in a
  variable keeps working:

```{r detach}
data_detach()
dim(cds)
sum(colSums(SummarizedExperiment::assay(cds, "counts")))
file.exists(count_dir)
```

* Saving a CDS that has a UMAP model writes a small copy of the Annoy index to the
  session temporary directory so that the staged files can be moved and deleted
  on Windows; it is not deleted, because the index may be in use.
* Failures are cached by projectData, which keeps a failed resource failed until
  `data_retry()`; see the troubleshooting section of
  `vignette("using-monocle3-data", package = "projectData.monocle3")`.

## Symbolic links and containment

monocle3 and BPCells follow symbolic links when they copy a matrix directory and
do not check where a link leads, so this package refuses them instead: nothing
inside a saved Monocle directory, or inside the BPCells counts directory being
saved, may be a symbolic link, and the BPCells directory must be flat with the
files BPCells writes. The library, the package directory and parents such as
`inst/extdata` may themselves be links. Resources written by `save_monocle_cds()`
never contain links. Base R cannot tell a FIFO or device file from a regular file,
so those are not detected.

## Contrast with projectData.Seurat

Both adapters use the same projectData contract, but their persistence mechanisms
differ, and the experience is not identical:

| | projectData.monocle3 | projectData.Seurat |
|---|---|---|
| Persistence | Monocle's native `save_monocle_objects()` / `load_monocle_objects()` | The adapter's own inventory and copy of each BPCells directory, plus `object.rds` |
| On first access | Rebuilds the CDS and **copies** the BPCells matrix twice into the working directory | Points the layers at the installed directories; **copies nothing** |
| Needs the installed package afterwards | Only for the UMAP index | Yes, for all layers |
| Conversion at save time | In-memory `counts` converted automatically | None: the object must already use BPCells directories |
| Storage diagnostics | None exported | `seurat_storage_report()` |

## Limitations

* Exactly one CDS per resource; the resource name is the object name.
* No persistent cache, no external file lifecycle manager, no explicit deletion.
* Saves must come from `save_monocle_cds()` (or an equivalent native save with
  `archive_type = "none"`, BPCells directory counts and no HDF5).
* `Iterable_dgCMatrix_wrapper` assays and `DelayedArray` assays are refused
  conservatively, without checking whether they would serialize self-contained.
* Saving is staged and rolled back on failure, but it is not a filesystem
  transaction: a killed R process can leave a hidden
  `.projectData.monocle3-stage-*` directory.
* The adapter relies on `BPCells::all_matrix_inputs()`, which BPCells documents as
  experimental. The assumptions about monocle3 and BPCells (the layout written by
  `save_monocle_objects()`, the BPCells directory files, the `matrix_control`
  interface) are stated by the package's `test-e2e-dependency-contract.R`, so an
  upgrade that changes one fails there by name.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
try(data_detach(), silent = TRUE)
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
```
